katie-sales: Hey team, ACME POC is seeing intermittent 503s when they ramp to ~120rps during the demo. Happened twice in the last 10m. They’re asking for root cause before the next call.

ajohnson: Thanks — can you paste the exact curl and any request_id from the responses? Also which model/route they're hitting?

katie-sales: Curl they used: ```curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-test' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"rdb-large-quant","input":"summarize...","max_tokens":512}'``` Response headers included `x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d` and body was HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable. They were on route `demo-acme-prod` and region `us-west-2`.

tara_s: Noted. 503s during load ramp usually mean short-term capacity pressure + throttling fallback. Can you grab a short log window around that x-request-id? If it's the burst pool kicking in we'll see `throttle=burstpool` or `autoscaler=delayed` in the runtime logs.

katie-sales: Pasted logs from their agent (redacted keys): ```[2026-11-21T15:04:10Z] req=req_0a1b2c3d route=demo-acme-prod status=500 detail="serve: queue full" host=gpu-node-7
[2026-11-21T15:04:10Z] req=req_0a1b2c3d runtime=runtime-3 action=reject reason=burst_pool_limit
[2026-11-21T15:04:11Z] req=req_0a1b2c3d status=503 user_msg="temporary overload"
``` They also included a timeline: spike from 20->120rps over ~30s.

jamal: I can see corresponding traces in our metrics: autoscaler took ~45s to spin up an extra VM group because their ramp exceeded the scale-up cooldown. Also GPU queue length spiked to 512 for ~20s. That matches the queue-full / burst_pool_limit.

ajohnson: Ok, two causes: (1) burst pool exhausted because sustained concurrency > configured burst size, (2) autoscaler cooldown + scale-up latency. Short-term 503s are expected under that pattern unless you pre-warm or increase burst.

katie-sales: ACME is worried — they expect demo-grade reliability. What are quick mitigations we can apply before the next call in 40m?

tara_s: Fast options: 1) temporarily bump `burst_pool.size` for that dedicated pool (we can do +2x for 1h) — immediate. 2) lower scale-up cooldown to 30s and increase scale delta so autoscaler adds capacity faster. 3) add a client-side retry with jitter on 503 for demo (3 retries, exponential backoff). I can apply (1) now if infra approves.

jamal: We can also enable emergency burst capacity (short-lived extra hosts) for the demo region; requires approval but can be done in ~15m. I'll start the approval thread with infra.

ak johnson: (typo) ajohnson: I'll prepare the exact CLI steps and required RBAC. ETA 10m. For retries: sample pseudocode for clients: ```retry(max=3){ resp = http.post(...); if resp.status==503 { sleep(exp_backoff()); continue } else break }``` This reduces visible failures for the user.

katie-sales: Sounds good. ACME also asked if this is a pricing/commit issue — they worry bursting will cost much more. Can you share guidance?

tara_s: For POC we recommend short burst increases; we can cap burst billing by setting `burst_cost_cap` so they won't exceed X dollars for the demo. Also explain that autoscaling reduces steady-state cost; the short ramp is why costs spike. I'll attach a one-pager after we stabilize.

deploy-bot: [autoscaler] scale-up triggered: group=swarm-us-west-2 delta=4 reason=cpu_queue_spike at 2026-11-21T15:04:20Z

jamal: Approval came through for emergency hosts. Spinning 4 warm hosts now, ETA ~8m. I also adjusted autoscaler cooldown to 25s for that group. Keep an eye on metrics.

katie-sales: Applying client retry as a stopgap and I'll ask ACME to hold the ramp for 60s after we signal. Can someone set burst_pool +2x?

ajohnson: Done. Increased burst_pool for demo-acme-prod by 2x and set `burst_cost_cap` to $150 for 1h. Patch ID: patch_20261121_01.

tara_s: Monitoring — queue length is dropping, 5xx rate fell to 0.8% from 6%. Will watch for next 10m and report back.

katie-sales: Amazing, please post a short summary for ACME and I'll relay during call. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ajohnson: Summary for ACME (sending): "We observed short-lived overload during a rapid ramp. Cause: burst pool exhaustion + autoscaler spin-up latency. Immediate mitigation: temporary burst increase, enabled emergency hosts, lowered autoscaler cooldown, and client retries recommended. Cost cap applied for demo. We'll follow up with a permanent scaling and prewarm plan"

munge: end of thread
